title: How Starbucks Really Makes Money (The Bank That Sells Coffee)
description:
The first Starbucks sold only coffee beans. Today there are more than 41,600 Starbucks coffeehouses, and customers keep around $1.75 billion of their own money loaded on Starbucks cards and the app. In this file we open the money machine behind Starbucks: the 1971 bean shop in Seattle, the Milan idea and the 'third place', the 2008 crisis, licensed stores and the Nestlé deal, the stored-value 'float' and breakage, the Back to Starbucks plan, the China deal with Boyu Capital, and the latest numbers.

{CHAPTERS}

Sources: Starbucks Q4 and full fiscal year 2026 results; Starbucks Form 10-K for fiscal 2025; Starbucks Q4 FY25 investor dashboard and Q4 FY26 earnings call; Starbucks coffee sourcing and Global Impact Report; HistoryLink (Starbucks: The Early Years); Britannica Money; QSR Magazine (Nestlé deal); Fortune / Bloomberg and Al Jazeera (China deal); NPR and UPI (2008 training day, 2025 menu changes); Sherwood News and Kottke.org (stored value).

All figures are rounded. Fiscal 2026 ended on 27 September 2026. Forecasts are company guidance. This video is for education only, not investment advice.
